summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease, type 1 diabetes, and bilateral lower extremity amputations was readmitted two days after discharge due to a productive cough, shortness of breath, and poor oral intake. She had recently completed treatment for Staphylococcus epidermidis bacteremia and was still on vancomycin. Chest X-ray revealed right upper and possibly right lower lobe pneumonia, consistent with healthcare-associated pneumonia. She was treated with intravenous Zosyn, which was later transitioned to oral levofloxacin. Her white blood cell count improved from 19.1 to 9.2 within two days, and she became afebrile with improved respiratory status. A catheter exit site swab showed sparse Candida albicans, deemed likely contamination; however, a two-week course of fluconazole was initiated as a precaution. Blood cultures remained negative, and she tolerated oral intake by discharge. She was discharged home with services to complete antibiotics and antifungal therapy, continue vancomycin with dialysis, and follow up with her care team.
